Formal proof of the 3D Kakeya conjecture

We're excited to share a major milestone: the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture now has a complete, machine-verified proof in Lean.

At Project Numina, we formalized the proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture in Lean from the Sticky Kakeya theorem, following the streamlined argument of Guth, Wang and Zahl. Nankai University and the ByteDance Seed AI4Math Team independently produced a sorry-free, unconditional formalization of Wang–Zahl Theorem 5.2 (Sticky Kakeya), the main input our development relies on.

Together, the two developments give an unconditional formal proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, with no sorry and no project-specific mathematical axiom.

  • Write-up: https://projectnumina.ai/article?slug=Kakeya
  • Github: https://github.com/project-numina/kakeya-3d
  • Sticky Kakeya formalization: https://github.com/M32026/3d-sticky-kakeya

Much of the code was AI-generated and, while it checks formally, it is not yet at Mathlib quality. We're committed to the long-term refactoring effort and to upstreaming the most reusable lemmas and infrastructure.

Discussion thread: #Autoformalization > 3D Kakeya in Lean
